title: Swarms, Edges, Phosphor, Gaze & Springs
description: Cursor agents that build a page, scroll-aware edge masks, CRT phosphor type, pointer-tracking avatars and four components on one spring.

drops.title: Agent Swarm Build-In
drops.description: A crew of cursor agents drags each frame out to size, sweeps a scan line down it and types the copy in.
drops.concept: Instead of fading content in, a shared canvas overlay sends labelled cursor agents to every element: one drags the border out from the top-left corner, a scan line sweeps taller boxes, then an I-beam walks the text and types it. The copy is never split into spans — the untyped tail is hidden with the CSS Custom Highlight API, so fonts, wrapping and ligatures survive intact.

interaction.mouse: Click anywhere to send the swarm out again.
interaction.click: Replay, crew size, speed and each phase (labels, names, scan, typing) are tunable.
interaction.touch: Tap anywhere to rebuild the page.

drops.title: The Edge Knows Where It Is
drops.description: Four gradient mask layers, one per edge, grown by a scroll-driven animation and cleared the moment you arrive.
drops.concept: Each scroller carries its own mask — not an overlay — so whatever sits behind it shows through the fade. A scroll-driven animation on `scroll(self y)` animates registered custom properties that size each band, which is why the top edge is sharp at rest and the bottom clears exactly at the end. Without scroll timelines it degrades to a static fade rather than breaking.

interaction.mouse: Scroll each panel; band width and onset are adjustable.
interaction.click: Drag the sliders to resize the band or change how fast it grows.
interaction.touch: Swipe the vertical columns and the horizontal rail.

drops.title: Phosphor Still Has a Look
drops.description: Four CRT tubes from one stylesheet — stacked glow, scanlines, aperture grille and a type-on that never reflows.
drops.concept: The phosphor glow is three text-shadows at widening radii tinted with color-mix, the scanlines and RGB aperture grille are repeating gradients multiplied over the glass, and curvature is faked with a radial vignette plus a rolling sync bar. The typewriter keeps the whole string in the DOM and merely hides the tail, so the box never reflows as it types.

interaction.mouse: Click any tube to retype it.
interaction.click: Glow, scanline pitch and type speed are tunable; replay retypes all four.
interaction.touch: Tap a tube to retype it.

drops.title: Six Shapes, One Pair of Eyes
drops.description: Avatars defined as one SVG path plus two eye coordinates, with volume stacked from cross-sections and a gaze that follows you.
drops.concept: Every avatar is a single path in a 0 0 100 100 box and an eye placement. Volume is inferred by filling the same Path2D many times at a decreasing offset and lightness, so any outline you can draw becomes a solid body. The eyes ease toward the pointer in each avatar's own local space, and six states — idle, thinking, working, waiting, blocked, done — change how the body breathes.

interaction.mouse: Move the pointer anywhere — every avatar looks at it.
interaction.click: Tap an avatar to flip its mood and advance its state; the panel sets state for all six.
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across the page to lead their gaze.

drops.title: Every Component Runs One Spring
drops.description: A switch, accordion, sheet and card throw as custom elements with no easing curves — just stiffness, damping and mass.
drops.concept: Four custom elements share one nine-line semi-implicit Euler integrator: force = -kx - cv, then v += f/m·dt, then x += v·dt. Because there is no timeline, interrupting a gesture keeps the velocity instead of restarting, and the spring parks and cancels its frame request once displacement and velocity both fall under a threshold. The panel plots the live step response of whatever constants you set.

interaction.mouse: Drag the switch, fling a card, throw the sheet down to dismiss it.
interaction.click: Stiffness, damping and mass are live for every component at once.
interaction.touch: All four are pointer-driven and work under a finger.
